Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat for Sale, What’s a 2024 MY Worth After 7,000 Miles?
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc
As every gearhead and their pet can tell you, the Hellcat engine is not dead, even if an AI tried to tell me otherwise when I asked it what models featuring the 6.2-liter supercharged V8 are still in production today, because these include the resurrected Ram 1500 SRT TRX and the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat.
Previous models included the numerous versions of the Dodge Challenger and Charger (the old one), as well as the mighty Jeep Grand Cherokee Trackhawk, but these are dead and buried, whereas Ram’s super truck and Dodge’s super SUV are still a thing. And we are here to talk about the latter. More particularly, the example pictured above, which we just stumbled upon, and as mentioned in the title, it is looking for a new home.
Before delving into the information that the selling dealer released on social media, which is more than modest, let’s talk about the appearance. This Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat sports a glossy black look on the outside from bumper to bumper, with only the red badging on the grille, front fenders, and tailgate providing a bit of contrast. The V-spoke black concave wheels spin around the red brake calipers, and the vehicle features tinted windows that do a very good job at keeping the interior away from prying eyes.
Fortunately, the vendor also released a few images of the cockpit, and unlike the exterior, it is more lively. That’s because it features red leather upholstery on the seats, on the lower parts of the dashboard, and on the center console. There is also black leather upholstery on deck, as well as some white stitching for more contrast, and the seatbelts are red. The SRT emblem decorates various parts of the interior, and the usual gear is on deck.
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc This Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat has individual rear seats, as we can see from the pictures shared above in the gallery, and does not seem to have any flaws. At least not when it comes to the visual part. Nevertheless, keep in mind that the driver’s seat is only partially visible in these pics, and chances are that it might show some wear on it. After all, the vehicle in question is not exactly brand new, as it has seen some action over the years, although not a lot of it.
According to the vendor, this thing had just under 7,000 miles (~11,250 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging. In fact, the odometer is said to read 6,933 miles (11,158 km), and you are looking at a 2024 model year example of the American super SUV that can give the exotic crossover establishment a run for its money while costing a lot less.
Since we started talking about the performance, we should remind you that the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat has no fewer than 710 wild horses roaming wild under the hood. The output is in brake horsepower, and it translates to 720 metric horsepower and 529 kilowatts. As for the peak thrust, it stands at 645 pound-feet (874 Nm). That’s how much the mighty Hellcat lump, a 6.2-liter supercharged V8, pumps out with no outside intervention.
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc But how fast is the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat? Well, it takes just 3.5 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, that is almost as fast as the usual performers in the blue-blooded crossover class from Ferrari, Lamborghini, and Aston Martin. These include the Purosangue, the Urus, and the DBX, respectively. The automaker says that the range-topping flavor of the Durango will eventually run out of breath at 180 mph (290 kph), and can deal with the standing quarter mile in a very cool (for such a thing) 11.5 seconds.
Now that we have revealed what we know about the pictured Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat , how much do you think this thing costs? As mentioned above, you are looking at a 2024 model year high-rider, and these used to have an MSRP close to the six-digit territory. Nowadays, they tend to fetch between $65,000 and $85,000 on the used car market in the United States of America. The latter sum is for examples with less than 5,000 miles (8,000 km) under their belts, in pristine condition, whereas high-mileage cars are obviously more affordable.
That still does not answer the question popped in the above paragraph, so how much is this one? Unless you said $84,995, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price at the time of writing. We found this Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat advertised on social media (Instagram) by @imad_mcc, with the dealer saying that shipping nationwide is available, and adding that it offers financing, and accepts trade-ins.
So, if you were shopping for a low-mileage Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat and saw this 2024 model year example, would you blow $85K on it? The 2027 MY SRT Hellcat version of the Durango has an MSRP of $81,495. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Imad (@imad_mcc)
